problem_statement: The emixs/ace-documentation site is a runnable Hugo documentation theme, rebranded here as Ledgerline Docs — the developer handbook for the Ledgerline ingestion SDK. Its documentation landing page carries a native Topic Finder: a 'Browse the docs by topic' panel with a category chip row (All, Getting started, Components, Guides), a live result readout, and a grid of topic cards that each link to a real documentation page (Installation, Usage, Alerts, Buttons, Panels, Collapse, Lead, Childpages). The same finder appears in a compact 'Browse topics' quick-nav block on the Getting started and Components (Shortcodes) section index pages. Three things are broken. First, the chip row is laid out as a fixed-width single line that does not wrap, so on a 390px phone and on tablet it is wider than the content column and pushes the whole page document past the viewport, producing horizontal overflow. Second, the finder is visually broken: the topic cards collide and overlap each other (shingled by negative margins) and the category chips render near-white text on a pale chip, so the chip labels are illegible. Third, clicking a category chip filters the visible cards but the result readout is frozen — it always reads 'Showing 8 of 8 topics · All' no matter which category is selected. Additionally the quick-nav block is missing from one or both section index pages. Repair the Topic Finder so the chip row wraps within the available width without horizontal page overflow, the cards sit in a clean non-overlapping grid with legible chips, the readout recomputes to the true filtered count and label on every click (for example 'Showing 2 of 8 topics · Getting started'), and the quick-nav block is present on both section index pages. Preserve the top navigation, sidebar section tree, on-page table of contents, search field, footer, and all existing documentation pages.
required_content: Repair the Topic Finder chip row so the four category chips wrap within the content column instead of forcing a fixed-width non-wrapping line.
Eliminate horizontal page overflow on the documentation landing page at 390px mobile and at tablet width, keeping the desktop presentation intact.
Fix the finder's visual layout: the topic cards must sit in a clean, non-overlapping grid and the category chip labels must be legible (sufficient contrast), not near-white on a pale chip.

Wire the category filter so the result readout recomputes the true count and label on every click, for example 'Showing 2 of 8 topics · Getting started', instead of a frozen 'Showing 8 of 8 topics · All'.
Restore the compact 'Browse topics' quick-nav block on both the Getting started and Components (Shortcodes) section index pages.

Implement the change in source files used by the Hugo build (the topic-finder partial, its stylesheet, and its filter script); do not edit only generated public output or hide content in comments, metadata, ARIA-only labels, CSS class names, script strings, image alt text, or console output.
Preserve the top navigation, sidebar section tree, on-page table of contents, search field, footer, and all existing documentation pages.
design_constraints: Use the existing Ledgerline documentation system: the Topic Finder must remain a normal-flow documentation panel that fits the docs content column and matches the theme's Bootstrap typography, card rhythm, and blue accent.

Repair the chip row so it wraps within the available width on tablet and mobile rather than clipping content or overflowing the page; a hidden scroll clip that leaves a fixed-width non-wrapping row is not a valid repair.
Lay the topic cards out in a responsive grid with no overlap, and give the category chips enough text/background contrast to read clearly.
The category filter is the graded interaction: selecting a chip must filter the cards and update the readout to the true filtered count and category label, live, on every click.

Preserve the surrounding documentation shell: top navigation, sidebar section tree, on-page table of contents, search field, footer, and all existing pages, and keep the 'Browse topics' quick-nav present across the landing page and both section index pages.
The landing page must fit desktop, tablet, and 390px mobile captures without horizontal page overflow or card overlap.
state_constraints: desktop_initial and mobile_initial protect the documentation landing header, top navigation, sidebar, and footer as regression anchors.
desktop_finder is the primary reference presentation of the repaired Topic Finder (chips, readout, and card grid).
tablet_finder and mobile_finder are the responsive discriminator states: the repaired chip row must not overflow the page horizontally at tablet or 390px mobile width.
desktop_finder_gettingstarted is the interaction discriminator: after clicking the Getting started chip the readout must recompute to 'Showing 2 of 8 topics · Getting started'.
desktop_getting_started and desktop_shortcodes protect the section index pages and must both carry the 'Browse topics' quick-nav block.
desktop_search_focus protects the theme's built-in search field and shared shell.

change_completion: The Topic Finder chip row is repaired so the four category chips wrap within the content column instead of forcing a fixed-width non-wrapping line.

The category filter recomputes the readout to the true count and label on every click (for example 'Showing 2 of 8 topics · Getting started'), and the 'Browse topics' quick-nav is present on both section index pages.
design_consistency: The repaired finder matches the Ledgerline documentation rhythm: docs content-column width, panel padding, card grid, and blue accent.
The topic cards sit in a clean non-overlapping grid and the category chips are legible with sufficient contrast, reading as a normal-flow documentation panel rather than a collided or washed-out one.
responsive: Desktop, tablet, and 390px mobile landing captures show no horizontal page overflow beyond the benchmark tolerance.
The chip row reflows on narrow viewports without clipping the category labels or the topic cards.
regression: The top navigation, sidebar section tree, on-page table of contents, search field, and footer remain intact across all states.
All existing documentation pages (Getting started, Components/Shortcodes and their child pages) continue to render.

author_notes: Native docs lever on emixs/ace-documentation (Ledgerline Docs handbook): a Topic Finder / browse-by-topic quick-nav on the documentation landing page. The topic cards reuse the theme's Bootstrap card styling and the FontAwesome iconography of the docs shell. Graded surfaces are the topic-finder partial, its stylesheet, and its filter script; the reference finder wraps its chips fluidly, lays the cards in a clean responsive grid with legible chips, and recomputes the 'Showing N of 8 topics' readout live on each category click.
